summary: New Zealand labor radical Arthur Desmond drifted from defending Maori rights and organizing workers to writing Might Is Right (1896) as Ragnar Redbeard, a racist, misogynist tract later mined by Anton LaVey and cited by the 2019 Gilroy shooter.

evidence.note: birth year and parentage unknown; host gives about 1842 here, later says 1859 appears in many sources
1884 parliamentary candidacy is his first solid appearance in the record
joins timber workers union, leads a maritime strike paper in Auckland
long segment on defending Te Kooti and Maori land against settler militias
flees to Sydney, labor agitation, Hard Cash and the Active Service Brigade
1904 Chicago standoff with police over his office side business, later acquitted
dies of a stroke in a Chicago bookstore, most likely in the late 1920s
extended reading of the book's passages on women as property
LaVey finds the book in 1957 and lifts passages into the Satanic Bible
Gilroy shooter, 8chan reading lists and the Redbeard Right white nationalist site

notes: Desmond's birth (1842 vs 1859) and death (1926 vs late 1920s) are uncertain; lifespan uses 1859-1926 from the packet's footnoted source. Covered span stops at his death: LaVey (1957-69) and the 2019 Gilroy shooting are legacy, so they set reaches_present, though the shooting frames both parts. A reviewer may prefer extending covered_span to 2019.
